content: Sodium selenite is a homeopathic medicine that has been approved by the FDA for use in providing digestive support following the removal of dental amalgam. Common adverse reactions associated with its use include nausea, vomiting, changes in nail appearance, loss of energy, and irritability. For adults, the FDA-labeled dosage for digestive support after dental amalgam removal is 5 drops, administered 3 to 4 times daily. There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of sodium selenite in adults, whether supported by guidelines or not. For pediatric patients, the FDA-labeled dosage for digestive support after dental amalgam removal is also 5 drops, administered 3 to 4 times daily. Similarly, there is limited information regarding off-label uses of sodium selenite in pediatric patients, whether supported by guidelines or not. There is limited information available regarding contraindications for sodium selenite in the drug label. If symptoms persist for more than a few days, it is advised to contact a licensed healthcare practitioner. Pregnant or nursing individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using this product. Additionally, all medications, including sodium selenite, should be kept out of the reach of children. In the event of accidental overdose, professional assistance or contact with a Poison Control Center should be sought immediately. Adverse reactions reported in clinical trials are limited, as is information regarding post-marketing experiences with sodium selenite. Similarly, there is limited data on drug interactions involving sodium selenite. There is no FDA guidance on the use of sodium selenite in specific populations, including pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Additionally, there is no specific guidance on its use in relation to gender, race, or immunocompromised patients. Information on the administration and monitoring of sodium selenite is limited. There is also limited data regarding its compatibility with intravenous administration. In cases of suspected overdose, the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) should be contacted immediately. The mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of sodium selenite are not well-documented in the drug label. Similarly, there is limited information available regarding clinical studies involving sodium selenite. Sodium selenite should be stored in a manner that protects it from light and heat. There is limited information available regarding patient counseling, alcohol interactions, and look-alike drug names for sodium selenite. The brand name for sodium selenite is PLEO SELENE®. If you have questions about alcohol interactions with this medication, consult your doctor.
